nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Powers the steppe grasses, reeds and the algae of the shallow, sunlit lakes.

nodes.name: Nura River and snowmelt
nodes.desc: Spring snowmelt and the Nura River fill the lake basins; water levels vary from season to season.

nodes.name: Shallow saline lakes
nodes.desc: Tengiz is a shallow salt lake, about 2.5 m deep on average, and the neighbouring Korgalzhyn lake is the northernmost nesting site of greater flamingos.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass, reeds, algae and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil and lake water.

nodes.name: Feather grasses
nodes.desc: Tussock grasses typical of the Kazakh steppe, grazed by saiga and marmots.

nodes.name: Common reed
nodes.desc: Reedbeds line the freshwater parts of the wetlands, and pelicans nest on islands or in dense aquatic vegetation such as reeds.

nodes.name: Glasswort and saltbush
nodes.desc: Salt-tolerant plants of the lake shores and saline flats; glasswort and saltbush were both recorded near the reserve.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Blue-green algae and diatoms in the lake water feed brine shrimp, midge larvae and flamingos.

nodes.name: Saiga antelope
nodes.desc: Nomadic steppe grazer that eats many plants, including some poisonous to other animals. Wolves are the main threat to adults.

nodes.name: Bobak marmot
nodes.desc: Burrowing steppe rodent that lives in colonies and feeds on grasses and herbs.

nodes.name: Steppe grasshoppers
nodes.desc: Grasshoppers eat steppe grasses and are prey for frogs and other small predators.

nodes.name: Brine shrimp
nodes.desc: Small crustaceans of salt lakes that filter algae; flamingos filter-feed on brine shrimp.

nodes.name: Midge larvae
nodes.desc: Larvae of non-biting midges live in lake mud and are eaten by flamingos and many waterbirds.

nodes.name: Roach
nodes.desc: A freshwater fish of reedy lakes, typical of the small and medium fish that Dalmatian pelicans swallow whole.

nodes.name: Mallard
nodes.desc: Dabbling duck of the shallows, eating seeds and aquatic invertebrates; huge numbers of ducks use the lakes on migration.

nodes.name: Greater flamingo
nodes.desc: Filters crustaceans, midge larvae and algae from shallow lakes. Korgalzhyn holds the northernmost breeding population.

nodes.name: Dalmatian pelican
nodes.desc: Fish-eating wetland bird nesting on islands or in reeds; the reserve is said to hold about a tenth of the world population.

nodes.name: Marsh frog
nodes.desc: Large water frog of the lake margins that eats insects and is itself eaten by foxes and harriers.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Opportunist that preys on marmots, birds and frogs, takes saiga young and raids pelican nests when water levels fall.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: The steppe predator of the reserve and the main threat to adult saiga; it also hunts marmots.

nodes.name: Western marsh harrier
nodes.desc: Raptor of reedbeds that hunts waterbirds, frogs and flamingo chicks across the wetlands.
